proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. In particular, floor(x) itself is an integer that is less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: This follows directly from the defining property of the floor function: floor(x) is the greatest integer not exceeding x, hence it is always ≤ x.
vetter_reason: The proof directly matches the lemma statement and is logically complete: it uses the definition of floor(x) as the greatest integer less than or equal to x, concludes floor(x) <= x, and then universally generalizes over arbitrary real x.
